LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is straightforward. All top-level code consists of standard variable definitions (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, makedepends, conflicts, provides) and a source array. The `source` array references the package's own declared upstream repository (https://github.com/vash909/WSJT-CB.git) pinned to a specific commit hash (`94f776d54946fe43db5e0bb9c966b1595c7b7d97`), which is standard and expected packaging practice.

There is no command substitution, `eval`, `base64`/`hex`/`octal` decoding, or any shell execution at the top-level scope. No network operations occur during sourcing — `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not fetch sources, and the source array entry is a plain string built from variable interpolation, not an executed command.

The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is normal for VCS sources and, per the gating rules, is not grounds to fail this step. The `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions contain only standard CMake/ninja build, ctest, and file installation into `$pkgdir`, but these are out of scope for THIS gate since they do not execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. None of the global-scope code poses a risk.
</details>
<evidence>

Top-level PKGBUILD code is standard variable/source definitions, no execution risk.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
